assumptions_challenged: Rodent intranasal biodistribution and efficacy reliably predict intact‑EV CNS exposure in larger species (NHP/large mammal)
A meaningful, regulatory-relevant potency assay and release specification set can be defined before selecting the therapeutic cargo/mechanism
An immortalized/clonal MSC source plus an MCB/WCB plan alone will deliver reproducible product identity, impurity profile, and potency across scale-up without additional process-validation data
Quantitative intact‑EV tissue exposure can be measured and distinguished from non‑vesicular label signal with the planned controls and analytics in the chosen species and tissues

Predefined numerical acceptance criteria for CNS exposure, PK variability, and absence of dominant non‑vesicular signal can be set that will be applicable across species and predictive of downstream PD/efficacy
falsification_conditions: Demonstrate, in a blinded bridging study, reproducible intact‑EV associated CNS exposure in a large‑animal species (preferably NHP) after intranasal dosing that meets predefined quantitative thresholds across animals and brain regions, with vehicle, free‑label, and disrupted‑EV controls showing negligible non‑vesicular signal; AND show concordant PK/PD linkage where the candidate formulation (but not disrupted‑EV or vehicle) produces the expected mechanism‑relevant PD signal in the large animal; AND provide validated analytics that distinguish intact‑EV signal from label artifacts with LLOQs and specificity acceptable for regulatory interpretation.

Establish a defined therapeutic cargo/mechanism and a validated, fit‑for‑purpose potency assay that robustly correlates with in‑vivo PD across multiple independent production lots and passage numbers, demonstrating lot‑to‑lot potency consistency within predefined release limits.

Produce an MCB/WCB-backed GMP process (upstream and downstream) with scale‑up runs showing reproducible yields, impurity clearance, and stability; release testing (orthogonal identity, impurity panels, particle/protein ratios) and stability‑indicating assays meet prespecified acceptance criteria across multiple batches.

Show that intranasal dosing in the target large species yields acceptable safety and tolerability at exposure levels required for PD, enabling that biodistribution/PD thresholds are achievable without prohibitive adverse findings.
strongest_objection: The proposed gate and minimum-definition plan assumes that (a) intranasal intact‑EV CNS delivery observed in rodents will be predictive for larger species/humans and (b) a candidate-like product can be meaningfully specified (release limits, potency assay) prior to selecting therapeutic cargo/mechanism. The primary objection is that cross‑species delivery uncertainty and the unspecified cargo/potency approach make the recommended candidate-definition and go/no‑go criteria premature and potentially uninformative for translational decision‑making.
